stem: Which clinic blood pressure reading meets the definition of hypertension in childhood?

options.text: Systolic or diastolic BP greater than the 95th centile for age and height
Any single BP above the 50th centile
Only systolic BP above the 95th centile
Only diastolic BP above the 95th centile
Any elevated BP regardless of age or height centiles

explanation: Hypertension in childhood is defined as systolic or diastolic BP greater than the 95th centile for age and height.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

rationale: Paediatric hypertension is assessed against age- and height-based centiles, and either systolic or diastolic elevation can meet the definition.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because hypertension in childhood is defined as systolic or diastolic BP greater than the 95th centile for age and height.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because the threshold is the 95th centile, not the 50th centile.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because either systolic or diastolic BP can define hypertension, not systolic alone.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because either systolic or diastolic BP can define hypertension, not diastolic alone.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because the definition depends on age and height centiles, not any elevated BP reading.
